info.title: OpenAsy Attack Surface API
info.summary: What your organisation exposes to the internet, from the domains you have proven are yours, and what changed since the last scan.
info.description:
Every screen of Attack Surface uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Every operation takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003). Only verified domains and ranges an admin added are ever probed: names found outside them are listed and left alone (ADR 0067).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Attack Surface runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Attack Surface origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_attack-surface_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Attack Surface is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

state.description: Only a verified domain is scanned. lost: it was verified, and its record was gone at the last check.

proof.description: The TXT record the domain's owner publishes to prove it.

anyOf.description: Why the last check did not find the record.

cidr.description: An address or a range in CIDR notation, at most 256 addresses (a /24 or a /120).

reason.description: Why the addresses are the organisation's. Kept in the audit log.

roots.description: The verified domains and ranges it scanned.

trusted.description: Whether the system's roots trust the chain.

nameMatches.description: Whether the certificate is for the name connected to.

headers.description: The headers the checks read, lower case: server, location, content-type and the security headers.

login.description: The page has a password field.

service.description: What usually answers on the port; not fingerprinted.

anyOf.description: What the server sent first, unasked.

key.description: The host name, or the address for one found in a range.

root.description: The verified domain or the range it is under.

anyOf.description: The address its ports were probed at.

id.description: The same exposure across scans: its rule, asset and port.

via.description: The verified domain or name it was seen with.

newAssets.description: Assets first seen in the last 7 days.

settings.description: How scans run, set in the environment (ATTACK_SURFACE_*).
